candidates.rationale: Ratio of the short-term (5v21) EMA trend spread to the intermediate (21v63) spread measures whether momentum is accelerating or decelerating; an accelerating trend attracts more follow-on buying/selling and continues, while a shrinking or sign-flipping ratio marks an exhausted trend about to reverse.

Distance of price from its own 21-day dollar-volume-weighted average price (a rolling VWAP), scaled by realized volatility: price stretched far above/below the liquidity-weighted consensus reflects transient order-flow pressure rather than new information and tends to mean-revert back toward it.

21-day momentum is discounted by how long ago the 63-day high was set: a fresh breakout (peak just made) keeps its momentum reading at full strength, while the same cumulative return earned while the actual high keeps receding into the past reflects a stalling, aging trend that is less likely to continue.

21-day price momentum is only trustworthy when backed by a genuine shift in participation, so it is multiplied by the 63-day change in average dollar volume; advances (declines) accompanied by rising (falling) trading activity are confirmed and persist, while moves on fading activity are unconfirmed and tend to stall.

A sharp multi-day move in the opening price, sized against the stock's own typical daily trading range over the last 15 days, reflects transient order-flow/liquidity pressure concentrated at the open rather than new information, and such moves tend to fade over the following sessions.

The classic short-horizon (3-day) overreaction fade is a cleaner, more reliable effect in stocks with a strongly established 63-day trend, up or down, than in aimless range-bound names, so the reversal signal is scaled up by how extreme the stock's medium-term trend rank is.

A linearly recency-weighted average of the last five days' returns, scaled by the stock's own realized volatility, isolates very-short-horizon momentum that is smoother and less noisy than a single day's move but far more responsive than an equal-weighted window, the horizon where continuation still tends to dominate reversal.

Counts how many of the last 21 days moved in the same direction as the net 21-day trend: a trend built from mostly-concordant days is a smooth, genuine drift that tends to persist, while the same net displacement built from a choppy, high-variance path is a weaker, less reliable signal prone to reverting.

A short (2-day) price move that coincides with a 21-day-high percentile of trading volume is more likely a liquidity-driven, climactic overreaction (block trades, forced flow) that mean-reverts, whereas the same move on ordinary volume is more likely information-driven and persists.

Today's trading range relative to the stock's own realized volatility flags an active volatility-regime shift, and this repricing signal is more informative in names whose book value has itself been unstable over the last several quarters (buybacks, write-downs, M&A), where price discovery is more active and range expansion is more likely to reflect real information.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. The (price - TS_MIN(w))/(TS_MAX(w)-TS_MIN(w)) position-in-range family failed correlation twice more (rho 0.875, 0.935) from window-only changes (5/21/42) and from a same-shape high-side reframing — saturated across windows, not just at the literal duplicate.
  2. RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(TS_DELTA($dollar_volume,63)) scored 4.053, beating the best fundamental-fundamental rank spread on file (3.405) — fundamental-minus-volume-delta spreads look more promising than pure fundamental-fundamental ones; try more.
  3. -TS_DELTA($open,3)/(TS_MEAN($high,21)-TS_MEAN($low,21)+eps) missed cheap_screen narrowly (|t| 0.93 vs 1.00) — short (3d) open-deltas normalized by 21d range are close to signal; retry with a CS_RANK wrapper or adjacent window before dropping the shape.
  4. ($open - DELAY($low or $high,1)) constructions keep colliding with Alpha101-family archive members (5-node overlap) — this shape is largely exhausted; only reuse it fused with a clearly distinct fundamental or volume leg.
  5. Pure price/return/range expressions with no fundamental or CS_RANK leg still dominate cheap_screen failures (7 of 20 rejects, |t| 0.23-0.83) — this includes $high-$low range/vol ratios, not just $return stats. The one price-only accept was a 21-vs-126-day $return spread scaled by 126-day $return vol (3.18); favor that short-minus-long-over-long-vol spread shape over ad hoc products of unrelated price stats.
  6. Fitness ceiling moved from 6.794 to 10.016 this round: the top 3 accepts were close's position in its own range scaled by its guarded 21-day close vol (10.016), RANK(|eps|/close) (8.430), and RANK(eps) minus RANK(3-day close return/close) (7.273). Push deeper into these three shapes and their niches before spending budget on low-yield territory.
  7. $earnings_per_share is now the single strongest fundamental leg (4 of 9 accepts, fitness 2.86-8.43), ahead of roe/roa this round, having been freed by a past eviction. Expect its easy niches (eps vs price level, eps vs short volume/return deltas, eps vs dollar_volume) to saturate within a round or two.
  8. RANK($accrual_gap) is a crossover magnet producing degenerate children: 3 rejects this round were crossover_not_a_fusion for sharing only the trivial 2-node RANK($accrual_gap) fragment with a parent (a bare +/- against one other simple rank). Fuse in a multi-node subtree from the other parent, not a single extra rank bolted on.
  9. Re-normalizing a volume field inside a denominator already keyed on that field doesn't decorrelate: CS_RANK($dollar_volume) vs raw $dollar_volume in the same guarded ratio hit rho 0.981, and TS_MEAN/TS_SUM smoothing both legs of an existing RANK(fundamental)*RANK(dollar_volume)-style product hit rho 0.910-0.915. Vary the field or window family, not the wrapper.
  10. For $book_per_share, a 63-day point change (TS_DELTA) is weak alone even normalized by close (cheap_screen |t| 0.84); the same window's dispersion (TS_STD) crossed with accrual_gap accepted at 2.963. Favor dispersion over point-change for this field.
  11. A guarded denominator built from TS_STD($volume, 21) collides with the existing volume-z-score archive block regardless of the numerator (archive_subtree, 5 shared nodes). Use a different window or a $dollar_volume-based dispersion in that slot instead.
  12. Swapping which aggregate (MEAN vs MIN/MAX) fills the same slot in a $close/$low/$high range-position formula doesn't decorrelate (rho 0.984) — vary which fields occupy the slots, not which TS_ aggregate summarizes one of them.
